solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}\log_8y&=x-2\quad(1)\\ 3(\log_8y)^2&=5-2x\quad(2)\end{aligned}$$

Substituting (1) into (2):

$$\begin{aligned}3(x-2)^2&=5-2x\\ 3(x^2-4x+4)&=5-2x\\ 3x^2-12x+12&=5-2x\\ 3x^2-10x+7&=0\\ (3x-7)(x-1)&=0\\ x&=\dfrac73,\ x=1\end{aligned}$$

Substituting back into (1): $\log_8y=\dfrac73-2=\dfrac13$ or $\log_8y=1-2=-1$, so $y=\sqrt[3]{8}=2$ or $y=8^{-1}=\dfrac18$.

$\therefore$ solutions are $\left(\dfrac73,2\right)$ and $\left(1,\dfrac18\right)$

\exfigure{1337_q34_s1}

In $\triangle ODC$: $\sin\theta=\dfrac x2$, $\cos\theta=\dfrac y2$, so $x=2\sin\theta$, $y=2\cos\theta$.

Area of $\triangle ABC=\dfrac{bh}{2}$ with $b=4\sin\theta$, $h=2+2\cos\theta$.

$$A=\dfrac{8\sin\theta(1+\cos\theta)}{2}=4\sin\theta(1+\cos\theta)$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: provides correct solution; 1: progress towards solution

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}A&=4\sin\theta(1+\cos\theta)\\ \dfrac{dA}{d\theta}&=4\cos\theta(1+\cos\theta)-4\sin^2\theta\\ &=4\cos\theta+4\cos^2\theta-4(1-\cos^2\theta)\\ &=8\cos^2\theta+4\cos\theta-4\\ &=4(2\cos^2\theta+\cos\theta-1)\end{aligned}$$

Set $\dfrac{dA}{d\theta}=0$: $(2\cos\theta-1)(\cos\theta+1)=0$, so $\cos\theta=\dfrac12$, $\theta=\dfrac\pi3$ (as $\cos\theta\ne-1$, $0<\theta<\pi$).

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline \theta&\frac\pi6&\frac\pi3&\frac\pi2\\\hline \frac{dA}{d\theta}&>0&0&<0\\\hline &\text{Increasing}&\text{Stationary}&\text{Decreasing}\\\hline\end{array}$$

$\therefore\theta=\dfrac\pi3$ is a maximum stationary point. $A\left(\dfrac\pi3\right)=4\sin\dfrac\pi3\left(1+\cos\dfrac\pi3\right)=3\sqrt3$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 4: provides correct solution; 3: finds correct $\theta$ values, including testing nature; 2: attempts to solve $\dfrac{dA}{d\theta}=0$, using the identity $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$, or equivalent merit; 1: differentiates correctly or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Let $3^x=u$: $0=u^2-10u+9=(u-9)(u-1)$, so $u=1,9$, $3^x=1$ or $3^x=9$, $x=0,2$.

As the area is below the curve:

$$\begin{aligned}A&=\left|\int_0^2 3^{2x}-10\left(3^x\right)+9\,dx\right|\\ &=\left|\left[\dfrac{3^{2x}}{2\ln3}-\dfrac{10\left(3^x\right)}{\ln3}+9x\right]_0^2\right|\\ &=\left|\left(\dfrac{3^4}{2\ln3}-\dfrac{10\left(3^2\right)}{\ln3}+18\right)-\left(\dfrac{3^0}{2\ln3}-\dfrac{10\left(3^0\right)}{\ln3}+0\right)\right|\\ &=\left|\dfrac{18\ln3-40}{\ln3}\right|\end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore A=\dfrac{40-18\ln3}{\ln3}$$
